tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Activate on requests like...'), focuses on user intent (reviewing sustainability posture, carbon footprint, etc.), lists many explicit trigger phrases and contexts (including indirect ones like CSV attachment or AI/ML workload mentions), and while dense, remains a tight paragraph without delving into implementation mechanics.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when a user asks to review or audit a workload's sustainability posture, carbon footprint, emissions, water usage, environmental impact, or resource efficiency. Activate on requests like \"sustainability review\", \"carbon footprint analysis\"..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with project-specific, non-obvious rules (API semantics, reporting lag, severity definitions, attribution logic) rather than general concepts the agent would already know. It avoids explaining what emissions or APIs are in general terms.
tests.evidence: Carbon for month M publishes by the 21st of M+1, so before the 21st the latest month can be two back. That is the normal one-month lag, not missing data.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (API call specifics, checklist of 29 practices, metric formulas) is delegated to references/ files rather than embedded in the body; the body only gives pointers and short critical rules.
tests.evidence: Load [references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md](references/sus-best-practices-checklist.md). For every practice, apply its evidence, NOT MET / PARTIAL criteria, severity and guard...

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown links in the body (workload-model.md, proxy-metrics.md, framing-and-attribution.md, emissions-collection.md, emissions-api-reference.md, csv-emissions-input.md, ai-ml-workloads.md, graviton-migration.md, sus-best-practices-checklist.md).
tests.evidence: Load [references/workload-model.md](references/workload-model.md). Walk the Agent Space topology...

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific step or condition that tells the agent exactly when to load it.
tests.evidence: ML / accelerated shape, or `Invocations` in the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace → load [references/ai-ml-workloads.md](references/ai-ml-workloads.md).

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consequential operations (CO2e estimation bans, read-only restriction, attribution ordering) are prescriptive with hard rules, while flexible parts (scope selection, topology walking) leave room for agent judgment with rationale given.
tests.evidence: Never estimate CO2e for a Graviton migration, AI/ML workload, token, inference or training run.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple data sources exist (API vs CSV export), a clear default/precedence is given rather than listing equal options.
tests.evidence: an attached export wins over the API for its metric.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable 9-step procedure for assessing any workload's sustainability posture, not a one-off instance; specifics like templates and constraints are embedded appropriately within the generalizable flow.
tests.evidence: Walk the Agent Space topology from the entry point, classify every resource into a layer, and record each resource's Region.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The 'Critical — read first' section functions as a dense gotchas list with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: Absent or zero emissions are below the reporting threshold (0.5 g CO2e, 0.5 mL water), not zero impact.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report and provides a dedicated template asset for it.
tests.evidence: Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Create one report artifact per workload...

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline template exists in the body; the report template is fully delegated to assets/report-template.md.
tests.evidence: Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Create one report artifact per workload, named `sustainability-review-<workload-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, with every section in order.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The sole asset file, report-template.md, is linked multiple times in the body.
tests.evidence: Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md) at Step 9 even when the user asks specific questions...

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link clearly specifies it should be loaded at Step 9 to create the report.
tests.evidence: Load [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Create one report artifact per workload, named `sustainability-review-<workload-name>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`...

tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The skill presents its 9-step workflow as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, and the detailed sections below reference the same step numbers (### Step 1 —, ### Step 2 —, etc.).

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 9 includes an explicit self-validation checklist the agent must run against its own draft report before presenting it.
tests.evidence:
Before presenting the report, check the draft and fix any failure:
- [ ] All 29 practices have a status, and every MET cites evidence.
- [ ] Every KPI and delta matches the collected data and the same 30-day window.
